subject: Deployment options & HIPAA/BAA requirements - next steps

Subject: Deployment options & HIPAA/BAA requirements - next steps

Thanks again for taking the call today — great to meet the MedTech Plus team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we heard
- You will be processing PHI (patient records + device telemetry) and need a BAA in place.
- SOC 2 Type II evidence required for procurement.
- Audit rights and long-term log retention are important for regulatory audits.
- Prefer private/cloud-managed deployment but open to options depending on timeline and cost.

Redwood deployment guidance (high level)
- Hosted API + BAA: possible for lower-volume PHI use cases with contractual safeguards and account isolation; default retention and shared tenancy constraints apply.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): recommended for production PHI at scale — predictable capacity, isolated GPU pools, better retention/observability options.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for the strictest compliance requirements — customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integrations, full audit control.

Ask / next steps
1) Can you confirm anticipated QPS / tokens per month and peak concurrency? (helps us size Dedicated pools if needed)
2) Legal: we attached a draft BAA for initial review. Please loop your legal and share any must-have clauses.
3) Security: we attached our SOC 2 package and HIPAA FAQ. Rishi can run a technical deep-dive to map controls to your questionnaire.
4) Proposed timing: technical sync week of Feb 27; legal review concurrently (we can provide DocuSign-ready BAA once redlines are agreed).

Attachments:
- redwood_soc2_package_v3.pdf (PDF, redacted SOC 2 Type II and control matrix)

Thanks Marissa — quick follow-up from our side after reviewing the notes: 

A few clarifications:
- We are a medical device company; PHI will be core to the workload (device telemetry tied to patient IDs). We need a signed BAA before any PHI is processed.
- SOC 2 Type II evidence is required; our procurement team will need to see the latest report and the control matrix.
- Audit requirements: our legal wants to understand audit rights and whether Redwood will support vendor audits / provide evidence during a regulatory inquiry.
- Data retention: we need access to logs and retention options up to 7 years for certain audit trails.

Initial preference: Private VPC (cloud-managed) or on-prem if needed — but we are sensitive to timelines and cost. If Dedicated with customer-managed keys and extended retention meets our controls, that could be acceptable.

I've attached our security questionnaire (MedTechPlus_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx). Our legal/procurement (cc'd) will review and come back with redlines. Procurement timeline is ~6–8 weeks once questions are answered.

Could Rishi or someone from security respond with specifics on KMS/HSM support, audit log retention, and whether you support customer-managed keys for Dedicated vs Private? Also, do you provide penetration test results or third-party attestation?

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Product Security | MedTech Plus
samantha.torres@medtechplus.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Torres <samantha.torres@medtechplus.com>, Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@medtechplus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment options & HIPAA/BAA requirements - next steps

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear questions. Below are concise answers; happy to go deeper on a technical call.

1) Deployment recommendations
- Private VPC (cloud-managed) — highest control: customer-managed networking, KMS integration (bring-your-own-key via Cloud KMS or HSM), and tailored log retention. Best for strict HIPAA environments.
- Dedicated — strong middle ground: isolated GPU pools + tenancy, support for customer-managed keys (depending on cloud provider integration) and extended log retention add-ons. Typically lowest friction to stand up compared to on-prem.
- Hosted API + BAA — feasible for limited PHI use cases, but default retention and multi-tenant runtime constraints make it less ideal for regulated PHI at scale. We can discuss isolation and contractual controls.

2) KMS / HSM
- Private: supports customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS) and can be configured with HSM-backed keys for encryption-at-rest.
- Dedicated: supports KMS integrations in most cloud regions; HSM options may require additional work with our infra team.
- Hosted: encrypted at rest by default; customer-managed keys available on enterprise plans in some regions.

3) Audit logs & retention
- Hosted default: 90 days.
- Dedicated / Private: configurable; we can extend retention to meet your 7-year requirement via an archive policy (object storage export + WORM if required) — will need to scope cost and storage plan.

4) Audit rights & evidence
- We provide SOC 2 Type II report, control matrix, and supporting artifacts where appropriate (redacted). We support vendor assessments and can provide evidence packages under NDA. For customer-led audits, we coordinate a scope and provide a point of contact.

5) Pen test / 3rd-party attestation
- We run annual penetration tests and have summaries/redacted reports available. Full reports are shared under NDA in most cases.

Attachments included: redwood_soc2_package_v3.pdf, redwood_hipaa_faq.pdf

Suggested next steps
- Technical deep-dive with your security/infra team to map our controls to your questionnaire (I recommend 60–90 minutes).
- Legal: review the attached draft BAA; we can iterate and produce a DocuSign-ready copy.
- I'll prepare an architecture note for Dedicated vs Private showing KMS and log flows.

On availability: I'm open Feb 27–Mar 3 for the deep-dive.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_soc2_package_v3.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB), redwood_hipaa_faq.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

Thanks Rishi — a couple quick procurement/legal clarifications from our side before we schedule the deep-dive: 

- SLA / uptime: do you have a published SLA for Dedicated / Private deployments? We need the SLA language to assess vendor risk.
- Subprocessors / subcontractors: will the BAA need to list subprocessors and will Redwood accept customer audit rights over them?
- Forensics / regulatory support: if HHS or an auditor issues an inquiry, what level of support do you provide (log extracts, eDiscovery export, chain-of-custody notes)?
- Encryption: confirm that traffic is TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest for Dedicated/Private.

We will pass the draft BAA to legal but would like sample language for subcontractor management and termination assistance.
